title: Windowed concurrency + adaptive pagination helpers for embeddings and rerank SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers integrate embeddings and reranking at scale and hit two common pain points across languages: (1) naive pagination + large batch sizes cause memory spikes or long tail latency; (2) insufficient concurrency control leads to hot shards and rejected requests. We need cross-SDK ergonomics for a) windowed concurrency (sliding-window style) that lets callers specify max in-flight requests, per-host throttles and backoff policies; and b) an adaptive pagination/batching helper that auto-chunks inputs by token/embedding-size and exposes a stable async iterator API in Python/TS and a channel/streaming helper in Go.
context: This ticket complements previous iterator and prefetch work but focuses on concurrency shaping and runtime-friendly chunking: - Should work with streaming responses and long-running rerank calls - Must be compatible with existing retry/backoff middleware and not duplicate state - Aim for consistent ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs so porting guides are straightforward
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs expose a single helper (name: WindowedBatcher or similar) that takes: inputs (list), max_in_flight, target_batch_token_size, max_batch_items, and returns an async/iterable that yields batches and respects backpressure
2) Helper integrates with existing retry middleware: transient errors trigger exponential backoff and do not deadlock the window

3) Python and TS helpers provide streaming-friendly adapters (async iterator for Python, async generator / ReadableStream adapter for TS). Go provides a channel-based iterator and context cancellation support
4) End-to-end example notebooks for embeddings + server-side rerank show 30% lower 95th latency under realistic load compared to naive concurrent submit + chunk defaults
5) Unit tests covering concurrency edge cases (max_in_flight=1, large single item, partial failures) and property tests for chunking stability
6) Docs + migration note comparing older pagination helpers and recommended defaults for medium/large workloads
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Spike complete. Implemented a prototype Python WindowedBatcher that maintains an asyncio.Semaphore for window and a token counter heuristic for batch sizing. Measured memory usage on a 100k-item synthetic dataset.

2025-02-18: Cross-language design sync with TS/Go leads. Agreed on API surfaces: Python async iterator, TS async generator with optional stream adapter, Go iterator returning (<-chan Batch, <-chan error).

2025-02-22: Added integration with retry middleware; shifted to token-aware batching to avoid oversized RPCs. Observed improvement in 95th latency but saw priority inversion when retries blocked the window; implemented retry queueing with per-request priority tags.
2025-02-27: Design review feedback from PM and DX: simplify default knobs and expose an advanced config object. Preparing PRs for Python and TS helpers; Go follow-up to mirror semantics.
2025-03-01: First PR opened for Python (draft). Bench harness scripts added under sdk-perf/ to reproduce microbenchmarks.
decisions: Use 'windowed' name to emphasize in-flight request shaping (WindowedBatcher) rather than 'prefetch' to avoid confusion with cache prefetching
Batch sizing should prefer token-count heuristics over raw item count because embedding cost correlates with token length; default target_batch_token_size=4096
Retries will be managed by existing middleware but WindowedBatcher will reserve slot until request completes (including retries) to avoid overcommit
Expose simple defaults: max_in_flight=8 for hosted, 4 for constrained Dedicated tiers; enable users to override via options object
tradeoffs_and_risks: Holding window slots across retries increases latency but avoids thundering retries; alternate approach (release slot on transient failure) causes retry storms -- chosen the safer path
Token estimation heuristic can mis-predict for languages with long tokens; will surface misestimates in logs and provide opt-out hooks for custom size_fn
Maintaining exact parity across languages requires small ergonomic compromises in each language to fit idioms (e.g., channels in Go). We'll document differences clearly
Backpressure behavior depends on consumer pull rate; users with tight interactive loops may need to lower defaults
implementation_notes: Python: implement WindowedBatcher using asyncio.Semaphore + async generator. Internals: buffer inputs, try to form batches by token budget, submit to client.embed() / client.rerank(), await response, yield results. Include cancelation via asyncio.CancelledError and context manager for clean shutdown.
TypeScript: implement as async generator with an optional ReadableStream adapter. Use a semaphore shim (p-limit) or native queue. Ensure node and browser compatibility for stream adapter.

Go: implement as two goroutines: chunker (produces batches) and worker pool limited by semaphore (chan struct{}). Return results on a results chan and errors on a separate chan. Respect context.Context cancellation.
All SDKs: add hooks for custom size_fn(input) -> estimated_tokens to allow fine tuning for domain-specific corpora
Integrate with existing telemetry: emit events for batch_size, estimated_tokens, wait_time_ms, retries so Console can build per-route insights
testing_plan: Unit tests: small/medium/large inputs, zero-length items, items that exceed max_batch_tokens; assert correct splitting and ordering preserved when preserve_order=true
Property tests: random item lengths and arrival patterns to assert invariants (no more than max_in_flight concurrent RPCs) using instrumentation counters
Integration tests: run end-to-end against staging inference stack with both embeddings and rerank endpoints using mocked latency profiles to validate 95th/99th latency improvements
Load test: synthetic plateau and spike patterns to ensure no resource exhaustion and graceful degradation (requests queued, not OOM)
migration_notes: For customers using older pagination helpers, recommend replacing manual chunk loops with WindowedBatcher. Migration guide will include code snippets for Python, TS, Go and a table of recommended defaults by workload size.
examples:
Python example (async):
from redwood import Client
async def run(inputs):
    async for batch in WindowedBatcher(inputs, max_in_flight=6, target_batch_token_size=4096):
        resp = await client.embeddings.create(input=batch)
        for item in resp.data:
            yield item
Rerank pattern: use same batcher but call client.rerank endpoint for groups (preserve order by passing original indices)
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: cancellation semantics across retries, telemetry events naming, and default heuristics. Check for any API surface that would be awkward to migrate away from later.
